summary: Dickwela Piyananda was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Catholic University of America, studying under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz (attested 1974).

Diego Loukota is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Hermann Berger at Heidelberg University. He taught at Heidelberg and served as Director of the Institut für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter George (1935–1985) was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Berlin State Library from circa 1972 to 1985, where he succeeded Wolfgang Voigt (attested 1985).

Dieter Gunkel is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at UCLA (circa 2004–2010) and held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA (2024).

Dieter Schlingloff is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied at Göttingen and Berlin, and held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University (1968–1971), Munich (1972–1996 as Honorary Professor), and Leipzig University (2005).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1970) under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and completed his Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He served as Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 2001.

Dilgo Khyentse (1910–1991) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Khenpo Thubga, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1987–1991).

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (1910–1991) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé, Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, and Khenpo Thubga.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Calcutta (1965–1977), Delhi (1977–1990), and Cambridge (1990–2008), where he became Professor Emeritus of South Asian Archaeology.

Dilip Kumar Biswas (1920–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, later holding posts at Visva-Bharati University (circa 1948–1953) and Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi (1914–2001) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University (-1961), and worked as a teacher at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel (1964–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held academic posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (circa 2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

Dines Andersen (1861–1940) was a Danish scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and served there as professor of Indian philology (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar (1907–1985) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and was Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Anagarika Munindra (circa 1967–1969) and Mahasi Sayadaw (circa 1967–1970).

Dipak Kumar Barua is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Dean of Postgraduate Studies in Education, Journalism & Library Science at the University of Calcutta (1987) and as head (学長) of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
